title: catalogue/v1, a module catalogue
description: A neutral, public contract for a catalogue of modules (brain.catalogue; packages/brain/docs/catalogue.md): its bricks (groups of modules), its modules with their hard and soft dependencies, what a machine needs to run each one, its estimated cost (RAM, disk, VRAM), its fallback and its licence; the distributions that ship them; and the presets an installer offers (base presets, and personas when a catalogue declares them). Any program may emit it (the Brain's brain catalogue emit, a product's own module manager); an installer or a settings tab reads it. Read tolerantly: a key this schema does not name is allowed at every level, so a producer may add one in v1 and a reader ignores it; a key it names keeps its type and its values. A new value of an enum, a new required key or a change of a named key's meaning is a new id (catalogue/v2). tests/fixtures/formats/catalogue/v1/ holds a document of each side.

generated.description: Who emitted the document, when, and from what.

by.description: The producer and its version, e.g. example-tool 0.1.0.

from.description: What the producer read (its registry, its manifests...), for a reader to know the catalogue's sources.

name.description: The catalogue's name: the product or the brain whose modules it lists.

bricks.description: The groups the modules belong to (a module's brick names one).

distributions.description: What ships the modules: a package, an archive, an image, the base install itself.

presets.description: The starting points an installer offers: the base presets, then the personas when the catalogue declares them.

id.description: A stable id, unique in its list; a label is renamed, an id never.

cost.description: What the module costs on a machine, estimated (0 or absent: nothing worth counting).

ram_mb.description: Resident memory while it runs, in MiB.

disk_mb.description: Disk it takes once installed, data excluded, in MiB.

vram_gb.description: GPU memory it needs, in GiB.

download_mb.description: What adding it downloads, in MiB (0 when it ships with the base install).

brick.description: The brick it belongs to: an id of bricks.

class.description: core: always on, no dependency beyond the base install; extra: an optional package or tool, no resident process; service: a resident process, local or remote.

status.description: planned: listed so a reader sees what comes, never installable nor in a preset.

auto.description: Used whenever it is found, whatever the preset: no switch turns it on or off.

ai.description: The module runs a model: what a preset that forbids AI leaves out.

components.description: What turning it on turns on, in the producer's own terms (the Brain: its capabilities).

depends_on.description: The modules it needs (hard): turned on with it; an id of modules.

uses.description: The modules it reads when they are on (soft): its fallback otherwise; never pulled. An id another catalogue holds is allowed (a note).

requires.description: Facts of the machine that must hold for it to run: a tool found (docker, git...), gpu, container_runtime, env:NAME; the facts' names are brain.status/v1's (docs/catalogue.md).

recommend_when.description: Clauses that must all hold for a recommended preset to add it: a fact (docker), its negation (not wsl), or a comparison (memory_gb >= 7).

fallback.description: What replaces it when it is off or missing.

licence.description: Its licence: an SPDX expression, or a name.

distributions.description: The distributions it needs installed: ids of distributions.

typologies.description: The project typologies it serves: ids of the typology catalogue; an id a reader does not know is kept (a note), never refused.

kind.description: What it is, in the producer's words: base (the install itself), package, extra, archive, image...

bundled.description: true: it comes with the base install, adding a module it ships downloads nothing.

source.description: Where it is fetched from and how it is checked; a reader with no network installs it from a copy with the same digest.

signature.description: Where its signature is, or the signature itself; how it is checked is the producer's.

kind.description: base: one of the catalogue's starting points (the Brain: lite, default, recommended); persona: a profile of user a catalogue declares, built on a base.

base.description: For a persona, the base preset it starts from: an id of a preset of kind base.

modules.description: The modules it turns on, whatever the machine.

when_fits.description: The modules it adds on a machine that holds their requires and recommend_when.

typologies.description: The project typologies it suits: ids of the typology catalogue; an unknown id is kept (a note).
